newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala 1996 GDP seen at 3.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala 1996 GDP seen at 3.6 pct.

text.p: Guatemala's GDP will grow by 3.6 percent in 1996, a downward revision from previous estimates of up to five percent, the central bank said Thursday.

"This contrasts with expectations that we had at the beginning of the year when we estimated economic growth could be between 4.5 and 5 percent," Willy Zapata, president of Banco de Guatemala, told reporters.
Guatemala's economy grew at an average rate of 4.3 percent from 1991 to 1995, peaking in 1995 at 4.9 percent.
Zapata said the slowing growth rate was due to structural adjustment programs that contributed to stability but restricted growth, and to reduced coffee prices.
Production of bananas, sugar, cardamom, beef, corn, beans and rice in the first half of 1996 was up from last year, but growth in industrial activity slowed, Zapata said.
According to Zapata, 3.6 percent would be a satisfactory growth rate given flagging growth rates throughout Central America and a 1.2 percent dip in coffee prices.
The bank president said inflation would remain within the goverment goal of eight percent to ten percent in 1996.

International monetary reserves in the banking system were $647.4 million at the end of the first half, up from $639.1 million at the end of 1995, Zapata said. He said increased reserves were a measure of confidence as capital returned to Guatemala from abroad.
